e.etymology: A short form of names ending in -rina, such as Caterina, Marina and Katrina, used on its own in Italy and elsewhere. It is also a Hebrew name meaning joy or song and a Japanese name written with various kanji.
The English bird name, from Old English spearwa. It was a medieval nickname and surname for a small, lively person and has been a given name since the 2000s.
namesakes: Captain Jack Sparrow (Johnny Depp's pirate in Pirates of the Caribbean)

assoc.t: the sparrow, a common small brown bird
Captain Jack Sparrow of Pirates of the Caribbean

e.etymology: The Latin word for peace and the name of the Roman goddess of peace. Angelina Jolie and Brad Pitt's son Pax, adopted in 2007, drew attention to it; it also works as a short form of Paxton.

assoc.t: Pax, cannabis and tobacco vaporizer brand
PAX, the Penny Arcade gaming conventions

e.meaning: denim, the cotton twill of blue jeans
e.etymology: A respelling of Denim, the fabric of blue jeans, whose name comes from French serge de Nîmes, cloth from the city of Nîmes. Denim appeared as a baby name in the 2010s.

assoc.t: denim, the fabric of blue jeans

e.etymology: A recent name used mostly in Hispanic families, shaped like the biblical names Adiel, Azael and Misael with their -el ending, God. It has no established source of its own.
A K spelling of Carly, a pet form of Carla and Caroline, the feminine forms of Carl and Charles, from Germanic karl, free man. Carly took off in the 1970s with singer Carly Simon.
A modern American spelling in the family of Amaya, Amiyah and Amya, built on the sound of Mya with an opening A.
A modern American name in the family of Sienna, Kiana and Tiana, usually read as Ci- plus Anna. It is sometimes treated as a feminine of the Irish name Cian, ancient.
A spelling of Qadir, Arabic for powerful or capable. Al-Qadir is one of the names of God in Islam, so the traditional full form is Abdul Qadir, servant of the Powerful.
The Spanish form of Amadeus, a Late Latin name built from amare, to love, and Deus, God. Amadeo I was briefly king of Spain in the 1870s; the usual Italian form is Amedeo.
The feminine of Hebrew Meir, one who gives light, from or, light. Meir has been a rabbinic name since the 2nd-century sage Rabbi Meir; Meira is its modern feminine companion.

The Hebrew form of Israel, the name given to Jacob after he wrestled with the angel in Genesis 32, read as he struggles with God. The spelling follows Hebrew pronunciation and is used by Orthodox Jewish families.

assoc.t: Yisrael, the Hebrew name of the State of Israel

e.etymology: A name from Cuba, usually written Dayamí, one of many inventive names coined there in the later 20th century. It spread among Hispanic families in the US in the 2000s.
The spelling of Eevee, the fox-like Pokémon introduced in 1996, whose name plays on the letters E-V in evolution. As a girls' name it doubles as a respelling of Evie, the pet form of Eve and Evelyn.
e.note: This exact spelling is the Pokémon's, and most people under 40 will make the connection at once.

e.etymology: From a Scottish surname for someone who lived in a glen, Gaelic gleann, a narrow valley. Glen and Glenn became first names in the 19th century and were at their height in the US from the 1930s to the 1960s.
namesakes: Glen Campbell (country singer of Rhinestone Cowboy)
Glen Powell (actor, Top Gun: Maverick and Twisters)

assoc.t: glen, the ordinary word for a narrow valley

e.etymology: From the Latin names Hilarius and Hilaria, from hilaris, cheerful, the root of hilarious. Medieval England used Hilary for men, after Saint Hilary of Poitiers; it became mainly a women's name in the 20th century.
namesakes: Hillary Clinton (former secretary of state and 2016 presidential nominee)
Edmund Hillary (first climber to summit Mount Everest, with Tenzing Norgay)

assoc.t: Hillary Clinton, widely known by her first name

e.note: The name fell sharply after 1992 and is still strongly tied to Hillary Clinton, so expect political reactions.

e.etymology: A spelling of Braden, a surname with two sources: Irish Ó Bradáin, descendant of Bradán, salmon, and an English place name meaning broad valley. It rose with Aiden, Jayden and Kaden in the 2000s.
A respelling of Piper, an English occupational surname for someone who played the pipes. Piper became a girls' name in the late 1990s, helped by Piper Halliwell of the TV series Charmed.

A surname turned first name, also short for Breckenridge, the Colorado ski town. The surname comes from a northern English and Scots word for a slope or a strip of rough land, related to Old Norse brekka.

assoc.t: Breck, nickname of Breckenridge, Colorado ski resort

e.etymology: A spelling of Edric, from Old English Eadric: ead, wealth or fortune, plus ric, ruler. The name survived the Norman Conquest as a surname and was revived in the 19th century.
A spelling of Samara, a name with more than one source: the biblical region of Samaria, the Arabic names Samar and Samira, and the Russian city and river Samara.

assoc.t: Samara, the ghost girl in the horror film The Ring

e.etymology: A Hiberno-Norman surname: Anglo-Norman fitz, 'son', plus Gerald, a Germanic name meaning 'spear rule'. Its use as a first name peaked in 1964, after the death of John Fitzgerald Kennedy.

assoc.t: F. Scott Fitzgerald, author of The Great Gatsby
middle name of President John F. Kennedy

e.etymology: From Sanskrit avani, 'the earth'. In India it is a girls' name, also spelled Avani. A separate Avni is a Turkish and Albanian boys' name.
A modern American coinage in the style of Aaliyah and Maliyah, with an initial N.
A recent form of the biblical Azariah, Hebrew for 'the Lord has helped', respelled with the E of Ezra and Ezekiel.
Of unclear origin. It echoes Azura, from the word azure for sky blue, and Zora, a Slavic name meaning 'dawn'.
A spelling of Jaden, a name that took off in the 1990s from the sound of Jade and Jay plus the -den ending. A rare biblical Jadon, in the book of Nehemiah, is sometimes cited as its source.
Probably a pet form of Marina, Latin for 'of the sea', and also used as a nickname for Marian, Mary and Margaret. Alfred Hitchcock's 1964 film Marnie made it widely known.
namesakes: Marnie Piper (teen witch in Disney's Halloweentown)

e.etymology: A modern American name heard as Ty with the ending of Bryce or Chase. Tice also exists as a surname.
Yiddish Reyzl, a pet form of Reyze, 'rose'. It is used mainly in Hasidic and other Orthodox Jewish families.
The English word for the state of being divine, from Latin divinitas. Its use as a girls' name is recent, alongside Trinity and Serenity.

assoc.t: divinity, the study of religion, as in divinity school
divinity, a fluffy white Southern candy
Divinity: Original Sin, role-playing video game series

e.etymology: From Persian zorawar, 'powerful, forceful', built on zor, 'strength'. Sikh families use it in memory of Zorawar Singh, a young son of Guru Gobind Singh who was martyred as a child.
